title: Senior's toolkit: pipelines from the terminal
summary: gh run and gh workflow: watch a pipeline, read only the failed logs, re-run what failed and fetch artifacts.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: pipelines from the terminal
steps.body: With the GitHub CLI (`gh`) you watch, read, re-run and trigger pipelines without leaving the terminal, and without scrolling through a web log of 5,000 lines.

toolkit.what: Recent workflow runs with status, branch and event. The quick answer to "is main green?"
Follows a running pipeline job by job until it finishes. Pick the run from a list or pass its id.
flags: exit non-zero if the run fails, so you can chain commands
toolkit.example: gh run watch --exit-status && gh pr merge --squash

toolkit.what: Prints only the log lines of the steps that failed. This is where the error is, every time.
Re-runs only the failed jobs, keeping the ones that passed. Saves minutes and runner money.
flags: only failed jobs (and the jobs that depend on them)
re-run with step and runner debug logging on

toolkit.what: Starts a workflow that has a `workflow_dispatch` trigger, with inputs. Used for manual deploys and one-off jobs.
flags: run the workflow from that branch or tag
toolkit.example: gh workflow run deploy.yml --ref main -f environment=staging -f version=1.4.2

toolkit.what: Downloads a build artifact (test results, a package) to your machine, to inspect exactly what the pipeline built.
flags: the folder to put it in

toolkit.what: The status of every check on the current branch's pull request, with links.
flags: keep refreshing until all checks finish
only the checks branch protection requires

steps.prompt: The CI run on your pull request is red. The web log is 6,000 lines long, mostly restore and build output. What do you run?
steps.explain: `--log-failed` prints only the steps that failed, which is where the error message is. Re-running before reading the error just costs another ten minutes.

steps.prompt: Match the command to the situation.
pairs: one flaky job failed; keep the jobs that passed
wait for the run and fail the script if it fails
start a manual deploy with an input
inspect the test report the run uploaded

steps.prompt: Re-run only the jobs that failed, this time with debug logging.
steps.explain: `--debug` turns on step and runner debug logs for the re-run only, without changing any repository setting.

steps.prompt: Main has just gone red. Put the triage in order.
lines: fix the cause, or gh run rerun <run-id> --failed if it is a known flake
steps.explain: Find the run, read the failed step, act, then watch the new run to green.

steps.prompt: Does the command only read, or does it start something on the runners?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When a pipeline goes red, read `--log-failed` before you touch the re-run button, and re-run with `--failed` so green jobs stay green. Use `gh run watch --exit-status` or `gh pr checks --watch` instead of refreshing a browser tab.
